'''Miwa Shrine''' (美和神社, *Miwa Jinja*) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in Miyamoto-chō, Kiryu City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a minor {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} and was formerly Ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA}} under the old shrine Ranking system.
==Overview==
Miwa Shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōmononushi Kushi-mika-tama-no-Mikoto|ja|大物主櫛甕玉命}} and {{ill|Takehayasusanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|武速須佐之男命}}. It is situated at the southeastern foot of Mount Agatsuma in Kiryu, facing Yamate-dori Avenue. The shrine is known for hosting performances of {{ill|Kagura|en|Kagura|qid=Q1348260|lt=Kagura}} and taiko drumming during the annual {{ill|Kiryū Nishinomiya Shrine|Kiryu Ebisu Festival|ja|桐生ゑびす講|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11537354}} held from November 19–20. A mikoshi (portable shrine) storehouse for the {{ill|Kiryū Yagibushi festival|Kiryu Yagibushi Festival|ja|桐生八木節まつり|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11537271}} is located adjacent to the worship hall.
==History==
Miwa Shrine is traditionally said to have been established during the reign of Emperor Sujin, with its deity transferred from Mount Miwa in Yamato Province. It was officially recognized as a shrine in 796 (Enryaku 15) alongside {{ill|Kamo shrines|en|Kamo shrines|qid=Q1306606|lt=Kamo Shrine}}. In 880 (Gangyō 4), it was awarded the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, alongside other shrines such as {{ill|Kamo shrines|en|Kamo shrines|qid=Q1306606|lt=Kamo Shrine}}, {{ill|Kohachisu Shrine|ja|甲波宿禰社}}, and {{ill|Oiwai Shrine|ja|小祝社}}.
The shrine was referred to as "Conferred First Rank Miwa Daimyōjin" in the {{ill|Kōzuke no Kuni Jinmyōchō|ja|上野国神名帳}}. Unfortunately, it lost many of its historical records and treasures in a fire during the Tenshō era.
Miwa Shrine was originally affiliated with {{ill|Enman-ji Temple|ja|円満寺}}, and both were managed by the Kojima family during the Edo period. It was designated as a Gōsha in 1872 (Meiji 5) and merged with the former {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|en|Yasaka Shrine|qid=Q692714|lt=Yasaka Shrine}} in 1908 (Meiji 41).

* '''Yagokoro-omoikane Shrine''' – Former precinct shrine of Yasaka Shrine
* '''Hata Shrine''' – Former precinct shrine of Yasaka Shrine
* '''Ichigami Shrine (Horinwa Gongen)''' – Former precinct shrine of Yasaka Shrine
